correctness.rationale: With the two named S5 relations and exactly the two atoms, worlds satisfying both atoms survive by reflexivity, and worlds satisfying neither survive vacuously. For an exclusive-type world that eventually disappears, its deletion round is one plus the greatest deletion round of an opposite-type witness in the relevant class (zero if none). At n singleton deletions the witness of maximal round for wᵢ, i>1, is necessarily wᵢ₋₁, so types alternate. In an a-class, different P worlds have the same Q witness set and would have equal deletion times. Every Q except a possible terminal Q is paired in its a-class with the next P, and a terminal Q cannot share an a-class with any P, since it would give that P a later deletion time. Thus all a-classes are precisely the required pairs or singletons; the b case exchanges P and Q. The constructed pairings give the deletion order by induction on surviving suffixes. The order and first type are recovered from the model, giving 2n! labelled models and two nonisomorphic types with agent and atom names fixed, also at n=1. If the relations coincide, any class containing both a p-world and a q-world remains intact and other classes lose only exclusive-type worlds at the first update, so the next update changes nothing.
residual_risks: Separate direct enumeration of all partition pairs and valuations for n=1,2,3,4 gave counts 2,4,12,48 and checked the full classification at those sizes. The supplied five-world computation was not independently replayed. The finite enumeration is corroboration, not the all-n proof.

value.rationale: The sharp n-round bound by itself would be trivial, but identifying and counting all models attaining it is a genuine structure question. The proof links the maximum-height deletion order to paired equivalence classes and explains exactly how distinct epistemic partitions allow longer dynamics than a single common partition. This makes the fixed operator a useful explicit example of extremal announcement behavior.
residual_risks: The result fixes the two atoms, two named agents and this formula. It does not imply a classification for general announcement operators, a formula-complexity theorem, or a census modulo bisimulation.
